subject.title: [Feature]: Per-agent cost budget enforcement at the gateway level

question: Should OpenClaw own native pre-dispatch spend-budget enforcement in core, expose a plugin/API seam for external budget systems first, or keep hard spend control outside OpenClaw for now?
rationale: The missing capability is source-confirmed, but choosing budget scopes, actions, storage, reservation ordering, unknown-pricing behavior, and gateway/plugin ownership is a product/API contract decision rather than a narrow repair.

options.title: Sponsor core budget admission
options.body: Define the minimal supported core contract for per-agent/default budgets, durable reservations and receipts, status/doctor surfaces, then implement behind additive config.

options.title: Expose policy seam first
options.body: Add a generic pre-dispatch admission/reservation API so plugins or external systems can enforce spend without committing OpenClaw to a built-in budget policy yet.

options.title: Keep hard control external
options.body: Continue improving usage visibility while recommending provider quotas or external proxies for hard spend enforcement.

recommendation.title: Sponsor core budget admission
recommendation.body: Define the minimal supported core contract for per-agent/default budgets, durable reservations and receipts, status/doctor surfaces, then implement behind additive config.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the strongest current-history owner across usage RPCs, session-cost accounting, agent config, and adjacent per-agent usage-cost work.
